articles.title: Victor Wembanyama takes strong stand against promoting sports betting
articles.summary: San Antonio Spurs phenom Victor Wembanyama has spoken out about a number of cultural issues. His latest was about the sports gambling industry.
articles.body:
Sports betting is everywhere. One place – or person, rather – where you won't find any support is with San Antonio Spurs phenom Victor Wembanyama .

According to the American Gaming Association, sports betting revenue surged to a record $16.96 billion in 2025, a staggering 22.8% year-over-year increase. That figure was bolstered by a 22% annual growth of the online sports betting market.

Despite the popularity, and despite the potential revenue Wembanyama could net, he's not interested in those endorsements.

"Absolutely not," Wembanyama told reporters Thursday, Oct. 1 when asked if he would ever become a brand ambassador for a sports gambling company. "I would never do that. Honestly, I think it's very sad to see some players promote it, in my opinion. Everybody does whatever they want, but without me."

Victor Wembanyama wins Defensive Player of the Year: See Spurs star in action

As the landscape for sports betting and prediction markets has exploded in recent years, several players have profited by signing deals to endorse these companies.

Recently, LeBron James ' previous deal with DraftKings expired, so he partnered with Polymarket. In February 2026, Giannis Antetokounmpo took a passive equity stake in Kalshi that is less than 1%, and he's doing promotional work for the prediction market. Boardroom, a sports and entertainment media network co-founded by Kevin Durant , has partnered with FanDuel , with Durant frequently appearing in ads and even floating proposed parlay bets that fans and users can tail.

The NBA also has a lengthy list of official and authorized betting and gaming partners , both domestically and internationally.

Can 76ers stars deliver a title? LeBron James says it's no 'instant oatmeal'

Wembanyama, 22, has repeatedly been outspoken about several cultural and societal issues, from his rejection of soda products, to saying he was "horrified" of fatal shootings of civilians by federal immigration enforcement officers.

Similarly, Wembanyama has expressed a desire to be very intentional about the brands he partners with.

"In the past, a dimension of money, but not anymore," Wembanyama said. "But even with that, I refused much, much more money than I've made for things that were not to my values. And now I want to promote things that have a good impact, have a good influence with who I can share messages and values. The one thing that's very important for me: our biggest strength is not our millions and millions (of dollars), our biggest strength is by inspiring. And we can inspire in a good or bad way.

"I want to inspire in a good way; that's the strongest thing I can do."

articles.title: Asian Games 2026 Medal Tally: Historic hockey, boxing, wrestling and archery golds power India into top 5
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India have moved into the top five of the Asian Games 2026 medal tally after a stunning day of gold-medal performances across sports.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India have moved into the top five of the Asian Games 2026 medal tally after a stunning day of gold-medal performances across sports.India now have 16 gold, 25 silver and 35 bronze medals, taking their overall tally to 76 medals. They are currently fifth in the standings, behind China, Japan, South Korea and Uzbekistan.China continue to lead the medal table with 162 gold, 81 silver and 73 bronze medals, for a total of 316 medals. Japan are second with 71 golds, 83 silvers and 85 bronzes, while South Korea are third with 33 golds, 39 silvers and 62 bronzes.Uzbekistan are fourth with 20 gold, 23 silver and 22 bronze medals.Historic hockey gold after 44 yearsThe Indian women's hockey team produced one of the biggest moments of the Games, beating defending champions China 1-0 in the final on Friday. The victory gave India their first Asian Games women's hockey gold medal in 44 years. It also secured a direct berth for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. Lalremsiami scored the all-important goal in the 10th minute with a superb tomahawk strike. India then defended their lead brilliantly to hold on for the gold.Sujeet produces stunning wrestling comebackSujeet Kalkal added another gold for India in the men's 65kg wrestling category after a dramatic final. The Indian wrestler defeated Tajikistan's Abdulmazhid Kudiev 10-9 after trailing 2-9 at one stage. Kudiev made a strong start and prevented Sujeet from attacking in the opening period with his arm locks. But once Sujeet understood his opponent's style, he used his speed and technical skills to turn the bout around.He scored eight points in a row and completed the comeback with a decisive takedown with around 20 seconds remaining.Sujeet then held on to his one-point lead to clinch the gold.Boxing delivers a hat-trick of goldsIndian boxers also enjoyed a memorable day, winning three gold medals.Lovlina Borgohain won the women's 75kg title, while Parveen Hooda clinched gold in the 65kg category. Ankush Panghal completed the hat-trick with gold in the men's 80kg category.The three victories gave Indian boxing a major boost and added three more gold medals to India's tally.Women archers beat world championsIndia's women's recurve archery team also created history by winning its maiden Asian Games gold medal. Ankita Bhakat, Kirti Sharma and Kumkum Mohod defeated world champions South Korea 5-3 in the final.The final was played in windy conditions, with the first two sets tied. articles.title: Man City Lodges 'Comprehensive' Appeal After Financial Scandal Guilty Verdict
articles.summary: Manchester City says it has lodged a “comprehensive" appeal of the independent commission's verdict. Here is the what and why of that appeal.
articles.body: Manchester City has lodged a "comprehensive" appeal, the club confirmed Friday, following the publication of a report by an independent commission detailing large-scale financial rule-breaking by the Premier League giant in one of English soccer's biggest scandals. "The club’s firm position," read a short statement from City, "is that, on multiple grounds, the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact and is unsafe." City has protested its innocence throughout the long-running case, which dates back to 2018 and reached a milestone Tuesday, when the Premier League published a verdict saying the Abu Dhabi-controlled club was "guilty of all charges related to serious breaches" of the competition’s financial rules from 2009-18. City has yet to receive a punishment. According to the Premier League, potential sanctions could be a reprimand, fine, points deduction or, in the worst case, expulsion from the competition. No team has ever been expelled from English soccer’s top flight. City officials said they would lodge an appeal and that was filed on Thursday evening, the club said, ahead of Friday’s deadline. "The club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case," City said, using language from previous statements on the case. The Appeal Hearing Should Be Over Within 12 Weeks Premier League regulations state that the chair of the three-person disciplinary commission that found against City now has to appoint a new appeal board. That also will consist of three people, one of whom "shall have held judicial office," the league’s rules state. The appeal board will then schedule a hearing that should finish within 12 weeks after the appeal is filed, and cannot exceed five consecutive days. That will be addressed in a separate, confidential hearing with the commission and there has been no word whether sanctions can be imposed before the decision of the appeal is reached. The Premier League has only said its intention is that the process is concluded "as soon as possible." City’s $1B Rule-Breaking Used ‘Sham’ Commercial Deals City was found to have systematically broken the Premier League’s financial rules for nearly a decade in what the competition’s chief executive, Richard Masters, described as the most significant disciplinary case in the league’s history. The investigatory panel found that City artificially inflated its revenue — using what the league has called "sham" commercial deals — by more than $1 billion from 2009-18 to circumvent financial fair-play rules that restricted rival clubs, and allowing City to buy some of the best players in the world. That was the foundation of a long and unprecedented period of success in which City changed the landscape of the world’s most popular soccer league, with the northwest club winning eight league titles from 2012-24. City committed almost all of the 115-plus violations, the commission found: 80 from 2009-18 for alleged financial misdeeds and another 35 from 2018-23 for allegedly not cooperating with the investigation. Source Of Sponsorship Could Be Appeal Focus City is likely to focus part of its appeal around the issue of how its Abu Dhabi-based sponsorship deals were funded. The commission found that sponsors in Abu Dhabi only paid 119.25 million pounds (158.4million) of the 949.94 million pounds (1.26 billion) stated in club accounts, with the remaining 830.69 million pounds ($1.1 billion) being paid by the Abu Dhabi United Group, the private company of Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan that bought City in 2008. Sheikh Mansour is a member of the United Arab Emirates’ ruling family. City contended that "no part" of the deals were funded by the ADUG and that, instead, the Abu Dhabi government — which owned the sponsors — had helped to fund the deals "from time to time." And so in City’s opinion, that source of extra funding was misunderstood, the commission wrote. The panel rejected that explanation by City as untrue, concluding it was "concocted well after the event" to disguise the source of funding. In an internal video to City staff — obtained by broadcaster Sky News — City chief executive Ferran Soriano said: "The whole Premier League case against us is based on a single false accusation: that the owner’s personal money was somehow and secretly put into the club via some sponsors from Abu Dhabi. This is just not true." English Soccer's Governing Body Comments On Friday, the Football Association — the governing body of soccer in England — expressed concern that the "integrity" of the game had been affected by the scandal. In its first reaction to the case, the FA said: "The independent commission’s decision has significant implications for the integrity of the game. We are carefully considering the decision and its implications and will take action where appropriate." The FA added that it would "continue to monitor developments closely" and would not comment further because proceedings were ongoing. Britain’s Tax Authority Urged To Weigh In The City case is currently a soccer disciplinary proceeding, not a criminal investigation. On Thursday, a cross-party committee of lawmakers called on Britain’s tax authority to assess the case. The chair of the Treasury Committee, Dame Meg Hillier, wrote to the permanent secretary of Her Majesty’s Revenue and Customs (HMRC), saying: "While I acknowledge that taxpayer confidentiality may inhibit what you can disclose, I would welcome reassurance from HMRC that you are seized of the importance of these issues and the public interest in the case." Manchester City Related StoriesGuardiola Standing 'Behind My Club' Manchester City Amid Bombshell ChargesExpulsion? Sanctions? What's Next For EPL's Manchester City After VerdictTimeline: How Man City's Financial Case Went From Leaked Emails To VerdictMauricio Pochettino: No 'Sporting Justice' For Tottenham In Man City Verdict In another example of the widespread impact of the scandal involving City, British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has been repeatedly asked his view on the issue. On Wednesday, Burnham said he would be "really concerned" to lose City’s ownership from English soccer, saying they had been a "huge partner in the building of modern Manchester" and of City as a global force, while also saying he was not getting involved in the process. Burnham was formerly the mayor of Manchester. On Thursday, Downing Street sought to clarify that the prime minister viewed the ruling as "serious and there can’t be any suggestion that anyone is above the rules." "If wrongdoing is established, those responsible should face the appropriate consequences," Burnham’s office said in a statement, which stressed that the independent process was ongoing. Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.title: Iowa HC Kirk Ferentz Makes Bold Comparisons For Ohio State Star Jeremiah Smith
articles.summary: Iowa coach Kirk Ferentz compared Ohio State superstar Jeremiah Smith to Saquon Barkley and Randy Moss.
articles.body: We're running out of things to say about Ohio State superstar wide receiver Jeremiah Smith, so, instead, we'll provide pro comparisons. Speaking at his weekly press conference, Iowa Hawkeyes head coach Kirk Ferentz — whose Week 5 opponent is the No. 5-ranked Ohio State Buckeyes (Saturday at 3:30 p.m. ET) — offered up a unique player comparison for Smith, specifically regarding his physical impact on a game. Jeremiah Smith-Saquon Barkley Comparison "There are several guys over the last 20-plus years, but the first guy that comes to mind would be [Penn State Nittany Lions running back] Saquon Barkley. Just different guys. They're at a little different level [than other players]," Ferentz, who has been Iowa's head coach since 1997, said when asked if he had a comparison for Smith. "The performance Barkley had against us [in 2017] is about as impressive as you're going to see. "I thought we knocked him out of the game. He took a hit and came back in a couple plays later. It's amazing. A really good player plus great toughness, and he's doing the same thing in the NFL." Barkley torched the Hawkeyes' defense in the two games he played against them. In 2016, Barkley rushed for 167 yards and one touchdown on 8.4 yards per carry, while also pulling off a 44-yard receiving touchdown in a 41-14 win for Penn State. Then, in the 2017 road bout that Ferentz referenced, Barkley rushed for a career-high 211 yards and one touchdown on 7.5 yards per carry, while also totaling 12 receptions for 94 yards in a 21-19 win for the Nittany Lions that saw them win the game on a seven-yard touchdown pass from Trace McSorley to Juwan Johnson as time expired in the fourth quarter. Barkley was a two-time Big Ten Offensive Player of the Year Award winner, leading the conference with 18 rushing touchdowns in both 2016 and 2017. He also finished fourth in the voting for the 2017 Heisman Trophy Award and was selected by the New York Giants with the No. 2 pick in the 2018 NFL Draft. In the pros, Barkley has won the 2018 NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year Award and the 2024 NFL Offensive Player of the Year Award — in what was a campaign that saw him become the ninth player in NFL history to rush for 2,000 yards in a single season — while racking up three Pro Bowl nods and helping the Philadelphia Eagles win Super Bowl LIX, among other accomplishments. Jeremiah Smith Accolades As for the 6-foot-4 Smith, the junior receiver recently became Ohio State's all-time leader in receiving yards and is coming off the best statistical game of his career. In a 42-19 win at home over the Illinois Fighting Illini on Sept. 26, Smith totaled 12 receptions for 217 yards and four touchdowns, which were all career highs. On the year, Smith, who's averaging 16.2 yards per reception over his collegiate career, has totaled 33 receptions for a nation-high 617 yards and seven touchdowns. He led the Big Ten in receiving yards in both 2024 and 2025, while leading the conference with 15 receiving touchdowns in 2024. Smith (34 receiving scores) is now two away from passing Chris Olave as the Buckeyes' all-time leader in receiving touchdowns, and is five receptions away from passing Emeka Egbuka as the program's all-time leader in receptions (Smith has 201 career receptions). Jeremiah Smith-Randy Moss Comparison Ferentz conceded there's only so much the Hawkeyes' defense — which is first in the Big Ten in opponent points (8.0 per game), third in opponent rushing yards (87.8 per game), fourth in opponent passing yards (152.0 per game) and fifth in opponent yards (239.8 per game) — can do to slow down Smith on Saturday afternoon, who also reminds the coach of a Hall of Fame wide receiver. "I remember, two years ago, getting ready to play [Smith and the Buckeyes] and watching a couple plays he made the week before where he's perfectly defended, and he still makes the play, and sometimes that's the way it goes," Ferentz said. "I remember being up at the New England Patriots' training camp in the late 2000s and seeing Randy Moss do the same thing on a red-zone play. I'm sitting next to the secondary coach, and he looked at me and just shrugged. "That's what great players do. If you can find a way to maybe make them play a little bit off their rhythm, that's a good thing, but it's easier said than done." After lighting up the Mid-American Conference with the Marshall Thundering Herd from 1996-97, the 6-foot-4 Moss went on to be a four-time All-Pro and lead the NFL in receiving touchdowns five times. Furthermore, Moss stands second in NFL history with 156 receiving touchdowns and fourth with 15,292 receiving yards. He was a first-ballot Hall of Famer in the Class of 2018. As for the aforementioned 2024 Iowa-Ohio State game, Smith was actually held to just four receptions. Granted, those completions went for 89 yards and a score in a 35-7 win at home for the Buckeyes. Ohio State-Iowa History Iowa is coming off a thrilling victory on the road over the then-No. 18-ranked Michigan Wolverines, as quarterback Hank Brown and wide receiver Reece Vander Zee hooked up for a walk-off, 16-yard touchdown as time expired, moving the Hawkeyes to 4-0 on the year. Prior to their Big Ten season opener, the Hawkeyes got wins at home over the Northern Illinois Huskies (40-0), Iowa State Cyclones (16-13) and Northern Iowa Panthers (55-0). Meanwhile, Ohio State has wins at home over the Ball State Cardinals (56-3), Kent State Golden Flashes (59-3) and Fighting Illini (42-19) under its belt. The Buckeyes' one blemish is blowing a 20-point, second-half lead to the now-No. 1-ranked Texas Longhorns on the road in Week 2. Ohio State has historically dominated Iowa, boasting a 17-3 record in the all-time series. With that said, the Hawkeyes were victorious the last time they played the Buckeyes in Iowa City, annihilating them 55-24 in 2017. articles.title: It's Unclear When Braves Ace Chris Sale Will Face Dodgers In NLDS
articles.summary: After Chris Sale recording the final four outs of the 6-2 win over the Phillies in game three of the NLWC, Sale's timeline for the NLDS vs. the Dodgers remains unknown.
articles.body: Atlanta Braves manager Walt Weiss reported to Truist Park on Thursday determined to avoid asking ace starter Chris Sale if he'd be available for relief duty only two days after making a start in the National League Wild Card Series opener. "I didn’t want to put him in that position because I knew that even if he was hanging, he would tell me yes," Weiss said. "So I was not going to bring it up." Weiss didn't have to worry. Sale was not going to make Weiss ask. "Literally, as soon as I stepped in my office this afternoon, he was sitting in the chair across from my desk, and he looked at me, and he said, ‘I feel amazing.’ That's what he said. I said, ‘Well, let’s talk.’" That talk led to Sale recording the final four outs of the Braves' clinching 6-2 win over the Philadelphia Phillies on Thursday night. Sale, the starter in Atlanta’s 5-3 win in Tuesday’s series opener, struck out Bryce Harper to end the eighth and closed out the win in the ninth by striking out Bryan De La Cruz and pinch-hitter Otto Kemp. "I was hoping he only had to go one, but he had to get to four outs," Weiss said. "But what a warrior, man. This guy, I’ve run out of superlatives for Chris Sale. Been talking about him all year. He’s one of the best I’ve ever been around. When you take everything into consideration; teammate, competitor, performer, work ethic, all those things, he’s as good as I’ve ever been around." Weiss said the discussion with Sale in his office did not include any mention of how pitching in relief on Thursday night could affect the left-hander's availability for a possible start on Sunday in Game 2 of the NL Division Series at the Los Angeles Dodgers. Even without the work in relief to close the Wild Card Series, four days' rest would be less than Sale was often given in the regular season, when he was 14-9 with a 2.16 ERA. Sale, 37, often was given extra rest and that helped him stay strong and record 200 strikeouts in 162 2/3 innings. When asked if Sale was an option for Sunday's game, Weiss said, "I don't know. I have no idea. We weren't even worried about that. We haven't even talked about that. We didn't look past tonight." The Braves had Sale and Tyler Mahle start the first two games against the Phillies. Mahle allowed only one run in seven innings in Wednesday's 4-3 loss in 10 innings despite suffering an abdominal pull during his pregame warmup. Weiss was concerned Mahle wouldn't be able to make the start and said Mahle felt better Thursday though still felt some discomfort. Reliever Ray Kerr allowed only one hit in 3 1/3 scoreless innings in the opener on Thursday night and likely will be part of the Braves' plans against the Dodgers. Kerr's strong performance against the Phillies was an important boost for the Braves' depleted rotation. "I was feeding off the crowd from the first pitch of the game," Kerr said. "They motivated me to keep going, throw even harder, throw even more. Every time I threw a strike, they were yelling, so I have to give it up to the fans." Left-hander Martin Perez would have been part of the postseason rotation before landing on the 15-day injured list on Sept. 24 with lower back inflammation. The Braves also have lost starting pitchers Spencer Schwellenbach, Spencer Strider, Reynaldo Lopez and Hurston Waldrep this season. Weiss said "There’s nobody on the planet that had us" in the postseason when the injuries included such projected frontline starters as Schwellenbach and Strider. "Nobody had us making the playoffs," Weiss said. "These guys have overcome so much. ... It’s guys like Ray Kerr and everybody else that step up and perform when the stakes are highest. It’s such a great group." Right-hander Bryce Elder threw off the mound on the Braves' workout on Monday before the start of the Wild Card Series and could be close to returning from the injured list after having surgery on his right knee on Sept. 7. Other possible options include AJ Smith-Shawver and JR Ritchie. Following games Saturday and Sunday in Los Angeles, the best-of-five division series shifts to Atlanta on Tuesday and Wednesday, if necessary. A fifth game, if necessary, would be played in Los Angeles. articles.title: Belichick’s UNC Staff ‘Inadvertently’ Signed Termination Releases Early
articles.summary: For all the uncertainty surrounding the future employment of the University of North Carolina’s football staff, the paperwork governing their departures is a...
articles.body:
For all the uncertainty surrounding the future employment of the University of North Carolina's football staff, the paperwork governing their departures is already in order.

A review of the employment contracts for UNC football staffers posted online by the university shows nearly all contain a termination-release exhibit signed on the same day as the underlying employment agreement. UNC tells Sportico this is not its standard practice and attributed it to a mistake by the football staff.

"Coaches have the option to sign the release in Exhibit A in the event of a termination for convenience," Kevin Best, UNC's senior director of communications, said. "Though coaches are generally instructed that Exhibit A is not supposed to be signed at the time of their hiring, it sometimes is inadvertently signed at that time."

The practice appears to have been a recurring trend of the contracts executed by head coach Bill Belichick. Of the 13 agreements for football staffers that UNC has posted on its athletic department website, only one—that of Bobby Petrino—does not include a signed release dated the same day they executed their employment.

In the case of Belichick's agreement , there are two identical signature pages—one following the main agreement and the other following Exhibit A, which contains the termination release—that are both signed and dated Jan. 22, 2025. The other coaches signed Exhibit A itself.

The significance of those releases has come into sharper focus following a series of coaching staff departures, including the recent resignations of football general manager Michael Lombardi and defensive coordinator Steve Belichick, Bill's son. Lombardi reportedly agreed to leave without receiving the buyout money he was due for a firing without cause. Steve Belichick, who also faced an internal investigation over his conduct, agreed to resign effective Oct. 27, following the conclusion of his scheduled medical leave that commenced on Aug. 6.

Agents of college coaches who spoke to Sportico agreed that this was unusual and inadvisable, though, as a practical matter, it might not amount to much more than a harmless oversight.

Brian Stanchak, founder and president of The BDS Agency, said that in situations where his clients accidentally sign a termination release prematurely, "I immediately request that those pages be replaced with an unsigned version."

Stanchak added: "In my negotiations, I always seek language that preserves the ability to negotiate the release at the time of termination. I even try to keep the coach's name out of the sample release attached as an exhibit."

Myles Solomon, head of coaches at agency MGC Sports, said he would not expect the chronology of the signatures to have a meaningful impact.

"Technically, signing the release too early could cost a coach their rights to challenge their termination on any sort of employment law grounds," said Solomon, who also directs the sports law program at the University of Georgia School of Law. "However, practically, I have a hard time imagining any judge holding a coach to a release that is based on an inadvertent signature."

UNC, 2-1, hosts No. 3 Notre Dame Saturday afternoon in Chapel Hill in a game that could prove pivotal for Bill Belichick's regime following last season's drama-filled disappointment.

articles.title: Social media reacts to excruciatingly awkward moment between Devils Jack Hughes and ESPN analyst
articles.summary: Jack Hughes' interview with ESPN's AJ Mleczko is already a frontrunner for awkward moment of the year after her injury joke fell completely flat.
articles.body: The NHL season is just a few days old, and it's safe to say that we have a frontrunner for "Awkward Moment of the Year" already. This one comes courtesy of New Jersey Devils star Jack Hughes and ESPN analyst AJ Mleczko. The Devils hosted the Philadelphia Flyers for their season opener at the Prudential Center. After the first period, the Devils were down 1-0, and Hughes was called over to do an interview with Mleczko, who was stationed between the benches. AVALANCHE FORWARD NATHAN MACKINNON SCORES A PAIR THEN DROPS GLOVES, MIGHT BE THE BEST PLAYER IN THE WORLD Hughes offered the usual interview platitudes and seemed to be pleased with how his team was playing. But then Mleczko decided to make a joke about the Team USA golden goal scorer's injury history, including an infamous moment in which he sustained a cut during a team dinner. WYNDHAM CLARK TROLLS CANADIAN OPEN CROWD WITH TEAM USA JACK HUGHES JERSEY, GETS SHOWERED WITH BOOS How did it go? Well, about as well as a dog fart at a wake. Cue the "Curb Your Enthusiasm" music. It's a rough one, and you've got a clear line of demarcation, with some going after Mleczko for making the joke. Others said criticism of her was misogynistic or saw it as an opportunity to go after Hughes for laughing at a joke the president made after the gold medal game. Personally, I think it was a perfect storm of awkwardness. Just an accidental mixing of social bleach and ammonia. I think Mleczko is a really solid broadcaster, and everyone has moments where they say something they wish they could grab out of the air and pretend it never happened. Any analyst who tried to make that joke would've ended up with egg on their face too. Buuuuuuut... Hughes is not known to be one of the more gregarious NHLers. If you make a joke like that, someone like the Flyers' Trevor Zegras or Florida's Brad Marchand would field it and probably volley one back in the other direction. I think Mleczko's biggest mistake was taking the wrong approach with the wrong player. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Who cares? Everyone goofs up. But it is also weird to take an awkward moment, tie it back to an unrelated and overblown moment from months earlier, in a vain attempt to build a narrative that just doesn't seem to be there.

articles.title: Seth Rollins Gives Update on Status of WWE Contract, Future With Company, Retirement Timeline
articles.summary: Amid his recent hiatus from WWE programming, Seth Rollins provided an update this week on his contractual status and future plans with the company.
articles.body:
Amid his recent hiatus from WWE programming, Seth Rollins provided an update this week on his contractual status and future plans with the company.

Speaking to Richard Deitsch of Sports Business Journal, Rollins said, "Right now, I've got three years left on my WWE contract—I'll be 43 when that's up. I want to be with WWE as long as I can continue to contribute and feel I'm helping the product, as opposed to taking up space that could be better utilized for younger talent."

Rollins, who is also a rising star in the sports media world as a guest host for Good Morning Football and The Rich Eisen Show , noted that he wants to continue fielding offers in that space as well while he is an active wrestler.

The Visionary added, "Once we get closer to the next contract with WWE, it'll be like, 'OK, what does this look like? Is there any interest from an ESPN for a bigger role or something that's more substantial, something that can provide for me after pro wrestling?' Right now, I'm very happy where I'm at and that I get to do both."

A six-time WWE world champion and one of the biggest pro wrestling stars of his generation, Rollins is still at the top of his game.

At SummerSlam in August, Rollins challenged Roman Reigns for the World Heavyweight Championship in the main event. Although Rollins fell short, he and Reigns stole the show with arguably the best match on the card.

Since then, Rollins has been kept off WWE programming, likely while the creative team figures out the most impactful way to bring him back into the fold.

Rollins has worked some live events during his WWE TV absence, though, most notably during the company's tour of South America last month.

With three years left on his deal, Rollins has plenty of time left to continue adding to his legacy, and his comments suggest that he may be interested in signing another contract when this one expires, particularly if it allows him to pursue outside interests as well.

articles.title: Shenzhen Open: Judd Trump beats Mark Selby to seal semi-final against world champion Wu Yize who edges out Shaun Murphy in Crucible repeat
articles.summary: Judd Trump whitewashes Mark Selby at the Shenzhen Open to secure a semi-final tie against Wu Yize, who progresses to the last four after a thrilling victory over Shaun Murphy.
articles.body:
Judd Trump whitewashed Mark Selby at the Shenzhen Open to secure a semi-final meeting with Wu Yize, who progressed after a thrilling victory over Shaun Murphy.

Trump notched five successive half-centuries against fellow Englishman Selby, but it was his composed safety play which helped him seal a 5-0 scoreline.

Selby had his chances in the first, third and fourth frames but was unable to compete with the world number two's cue-ball control.

World champion Wu made two centuries in the last three frames to edge a 5-4 victory over Murphy in a repeat of this year's Crucible final, which the Chinese player also won in a deciding frame.

Murphy had breaks of 104 and 98, but these came in between frames where he fluffed straightforward pots, allowing Wu to go into the interval on level terms.

The 44-year-old Englishman went 3-2 up thanks to a break of 68, only for Wu to produce impressive breaks of his own - 94 and 121 - to get his nose in front.

In an error-strewn eighth frame, Murphy was able to draw level after Wu missed a crucial brown, but the 22-year-old capitalised on a mistake in the decider with a break of 117.

Elsewhere, world number 45 Jimmy Robertson claimed a 5-3 win over Chris Wakelin to keep alive his hopes of a first ranking title since 2018.

He will next face China's Yuan Sijun, who rattled off four frames in a row, including two centuries, as he fought back to claim a 5-2 win over Michael Holt.

articles.standfirst: Las cuatro primeras parejas del ranking cumplen los pronósticos y pelearán en el recinto Ahoy por los dos billetes a la gran final
articles.summary: Las cuatro primeras parejas del ranking cumplen los pronósticos y pelearán en el recinto Ahoy por los dos billetes a la gran final
articles.body: Las cuatro duplas de la parte alta del escalafón FIP no fallaron en la jornada de cuartos de final del Rotterdam P2. Las número uno, Gemma Triay y Delfi Brea, volverán a medirse a las vigentes campeonas del Paris Major, Ari Sánchez y Andrea Ustero, mientras que Claudia Fernández y Martina Calvo afrontarán un nuevo compromiso de máxima exigencia ante Paula Josemaría y Bea González en la búsqueda de la final. Las únicas cabezas de serie que se vieron obligadas a acudir al tercer set fueron precisamente Josemaría y González. La extremeña y la malagueña tenían la oportunidad de tomarse la revancha ante Sofía Araújo y Marta Ortega, quienes las habían eliminado en la cita anterior de París. El arranque favoreció a la madrileña y la portuguesa, que tomaron la delantera al adjudicarse la primera manga por 6-4. Sin embargo, las jugadoras dirigidas por Claudio Gilardoni reaccionaron en el segundo parcial (6-3) y mantuvieron la inercia positiva para certificar el triunfo con un 6-2 final, sellando su regreso a la penúltima ronda de un torneo de categoría P2. En semifinales se medirán a Claudia Fernández y Martina Calvo. La madrileña y la navarra avanzaron tras superar en cuartos de final a Claudia Jensen y a su compañera circunstancial, la joven española Claudia Escacena, por 6-3 y 7-5. El balance de enfrentamientos directos entre ambas duplas refleja una notable paridad, con triunfos repartidos, pero con Claudia y Martina siendo las dominadoras de cada duelo. Por el otro lado del cuadro, Ari Sánchez y Andrea Ustero confirmaron su momento de forma tras conquistar el título en la Pista Philippe Chatrier hace dos semanas. La reusense y la barcelonesa superaron sin sobresaltos su cruce de cuartos de final frente a Julieta Bidahorria y Virginia Riera —pareja que venía de eliminar a Alejandra Alonso y Marina Guinart— con un resultado de 6-3 y 6-2. Por su parte, las número uno del ranking, Gemma Triay y Delfi Brea, firmaron una actuación categórica para certificar su presencia en las semifinales. La menorquina y la argentina se impusieron a Alejandra Salazar y Aranza Osoro arrancando el choque con un 6-0 en el primer set y cerrando el duelo en la segunda manga por 6-4. Las semifinales femeninas del Rotterdam P2 abrirán la jornada de este sábado en el recinto Ahoy, en un torneo clave para el devenir de la Race y las posiciones de privilegio del circuito Premier Padel.

articles.body:

Action in the Nations League continues this weekend with a matchday three tie between Croatia and England.

With a win and a defeat each, Croatia and England have both made a mixed start to this year’s competition.

Drawn in a group alongside the reigning world champions Spain and minnows Czechia, Croatia and England find themselves in an interesting yet challenging pool.

Captain Harry Kane has led from the front for the Three Lions, excelling in front of goal alongside winger Anthony Gordon, while Luka Modric continues to defy age, still playing a vital role in Croatia’s midfield even at 41.

Al Jazeera breaks down everything ahead of Croatia vs England:

The UEFA Nations League was founded in 2018 to reduce the number of meaningless friendlies and give nations competitive matches against top-ranked teams.

In this competition, countries from across Europe participate in a league structure which features promotion and relegation.

How have Croatia and England played in the Nations League?

Both Croatia and England have won once and lost once.

Croatia started their Nations League campaign with a 2-1 win over Czechia in Prague before losing 4-1 to world champions Spain in Seville.

England, on the other hand, fell 3-2 to Spain in their campaign opener in London before beating a 10-man Czechia side 2-0 in Prague.

They last met at the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

England beat Croatia 4-2 in a World Cup group game on June 17 in Arlington, Texas. Captain Harry Kane scored a brace, while Marcus Rashford and Jude Bellingham scored a goal apiece.

Time and again, the captain has pulled the strings in the middle of the park, proving age is just a number. His fellow experienced teammate, Perisic, is also chipping in style, bagging back-to-back assists.

Harry Kane and Anthony Gordon (England): The script for England has looked the same in the last two games: Gordon opens the scoring, and Kane follows suit. While that wasn’t enough to beat the mighty Spain, it did the job against Czechia. Can this dynamic duo strike again? The numbers swing in their favour – Gordon has five assists already for Barcelona this season, while Kane has scored six times for Bayern Munich.

articles.title: Allison Fisher: Pool pioneer retiring from professional competition after being diagnosed with Parkinson's disease
articles.summary: Seven-time World Women's Snooker champion Allison Fisher is retiring from cue sports after sharing the news that she has been diagnosed with Parkinson's disease
articles.body:
'The Duchess of Doom' is widely regarded as the greatest female pool player of all time and one of the greatest female snooker players.

She rose to prominence as a dominant force in women's snooker before moving to the US in 1995 to play on the pool circuit.

Speaking on social media, Fisher, who was awarded an MBE in 2022 for her services to sport, said: "I have some deeply personal news that I'm now ready to share. Last year, I was diagnosed with the early stages of Parkinson's disease.

"I chose to keep my diagnosis private for a while because I needed time to process what it meant for me, my life and, of course, my career.

"Cue sports have been such an enormous part of my life. I've been incredibly fortunate to play the game I love at the highest level for so many years, travel the world, compete against amazing players and make friendships that will last a lifetime.

"As Parkinson's has begun to affect the precision I need to compete at the highest level, I have made the very difficult decision to retire from professional competition.

"This may be the end of one chapter, but it is certainly not the end of my journey in cue sports.

"I still love this game as much as I ever have, and I plan to remain very much a part of it - through teaching, commentary, Legends of the Cue, appearances and other projects that I look forward to sharing with you.

"You can read more about my diagnosis and my decision in the latest issue of Billiards Digest and hear more from me on Legends of the Cue.

"Most importantly, I want to thank everyone who has supported me throughout my career. The messages, friendships, memories and encouragement have meant more to me than you may ever know. There is still much more ahead."

Fisher won the World Women's Snooker Championship for the first time following a 5-1 defeat of Stacey Hillyard in 1985.

She would go on to claim the title on seven occasions with her final crown coming in 1994 against the same opponent.

articles.title: World Grand Prix: James Wade thrashes Gian van Veen to book Luke Humphries semi-final after Gerwyn Price edges thriller
articles.summary: Luke Humphries beat Niels Zonneveld to book a semi-final meeting with James Wade, while Nathan Aspinall will play Gerwyn Price in the last four; watch the World Grand Prix semi-finals live on Saturday from 8pm on Sky Sports+ and 8.30pm on Sky Sports Main Event
articles.body:
Price battled back from two sets down in an absorbing all-Welsh contest at the Mattioli Arena, where he won six of the next seven legs to level the match before Clayton edged ahead in a dramatic final set.

Clayton missed a match dart to win the set in straight legs and saw Price drag the contest into a last-leg decider, where 'The Ferret' wasted two more match-winning darts to allow his compatriot to snatch victory and a semi-final spot.

Price will face Nathan Aspinall, who fired a 105.15 average - the fourth highest in World Grand Prix history and best in a quarter-final - during his straight-sets win over Ryan Joyce, with the other two matches also offering big storylines.

Wade dropped one leg during a one-sided victory against third seed Van Veen while Luke Humphries - the favourite after Luke Littler's shock early exit - has yet to lose a set after brushing aside Niels Zonneveld 3-0 in the final match.

Price's comeback win sets up Aspinall semi

A year on from blowing a two-set lead and losing a quarter-final in a deciding leg to Littler, Price produced his own comeback to book a fifth World Grand Prix semi-final in seven years.

Clayton took out 110 and 117 before surviving set darts to sneak the opening in a last leg, then took the next in straight legs but saw Price open the third with an 11-dart break and 12-dart hold.

Price averaged over 107 during the third set and breezed through the fourth to set up a decider, where he recovered from losing the next two legs and missed opportunities from Clayton to complete a memorable victory.

"I know what it's like to be in front and losing, but I feel like I was the better player all the way through the game," Price told Sky Sports . "I'm just glad I got over the winning line. I thought I was dead and buried, but I never gave up."

The opening match of the evening saw Aspinall race through the opening set in just 42 darts and take out 110 to claim a fourth straight leg to start the second, where Joyce needed to fire a stunning 153 checkout just to hold throw.

Aspinall nailed a 112 finish on his way to closing out the second set and broke early in the third to move closer to victory, with Joyce missing two set darts before seeing 'The Asp' close out a convincing win by taking out 75.

"I'm really happy with that performance," Aspinall told Sky Sports , having reached the semi-finals for the first time since 2022. "My starting, my finishing, my 180s - it's probably one of my best performances ever on stage for my whole career.

"I feel like I can win this tournament, and I feel like I'm ready to win another major again. There's no reason why I can't and I'd love to win the trophy on Sunday."

Wade books Humphries showdown in Leicester

Van Veen said pre-match that he felt Wade may be the favourite for their quarter-final, with the Dutchman delivering a sub-standard performance as 'The Machine' raced into the last four for the first time since 2014.

Wade won each of the first eight legs and didn't allow Van Veen a dart at double until the third set, where he converted at the fourth attempt to claim his only leg of the contest, but the sixth seed held throw on tops in the next to complete a 3-0 win.

"I was really fortunate Gian played like he did," Wade told Sky Sports . "He was pretty poor and I capitalised on that and bashed him up. Tonight, I felt more up for it. When I'm feeling up for it, I've done alright."

Wade will face 2023 winner Humphries, who has still yet to reach his desired level despite following straight-sets wins over Dave Chisnall and Jermaine Wattimena by claiming another victory without dropping a set.

Zonneveld missed a set dart to level the match before Humphries opened up a two-set cushion, with the world No 2 only converting 31 per cent of doubles but delivering a string of clutch finishes in tight legs during his latest 3-0 win.

"It's one of those performance where you aren't thrilled, but you win 3-0," Humphries told Sky Sports .

"Hopefully tomorrow is a lot better because if it isn't, I won't be here on Sunday. If I score the way I know I can, then it will be a tough night for James. If I don't, it's going to be a tough night for myself."

articles.standfirst: La pareja número cinco derrotó a los número dos por un doble 6-4 y disputará sus primeras semifinales como dupla
articles.summary: La pareja número cinco derrotó a los número dos por un doble 6-4 y disputará sus primeras semifinales como dupla
articles.body: Jon Sanz y Franco Stupaczuk firmaron la gran sorpresa del P2 de Rotterdam tras eliminar a Ale Galán y Fede Chingotto en la ronda de cuartos de final. El triunfo clasifica por primera vez a las semifinales de un torneo de Premier Padel a la dupla hispano-argentina, frenando la aspiración de la pareja número dos de recortar distancias en el ranking con los líderes de la clasificación general. Sanz y Stupaczuk afrontaban el compromiso tras ceder la cuarta posición del ranking en el Paris Major ante Paquito Navarro y Martín Di Nenno, además de haber alcanzado la final en el reciente FIP Platinum de Lyon. Por su parte, Galán y Chingotto partían con la regularidad como aval habitual en sus actuaciones, sin haber cedido en rondas previas a semifinales en los torneos disputados durante el presente curso. Sin embargo, el navarro y el chaqueño mantuvieron la paridad en los primeros juegos del choque y aprovecharon un quiebre en los compases finales para adjudicarse el primer set por 6-4. En el segundo parcial, Sanz y Stupaczuk tomaron ventaja nuevamente desde el resto. Aunque Galán y Chingotto lograron recuperar el quiebre de desventaja para igualar el marcador, Sanz y Stupaczuk volvieron a romper el servicio rival en el juego posterior y cerraron el encuentro con un nuevo 6-4. En el turno anterior, Arturo Coello y Agustín Tapia necesitaron tres sets para resolver su cruce frente a Gonzalo Alfonso y Valentino Libaak. La pareja argentina se adjudicó la primera manga por 6-4 aprovechando las imprecisiones de los cabezas de serie número uno. No obstante, Coello y Tapia reaccionaron en el segundo parcial (6-3) y mantuvieron el control en el set decisivo para abrochar el triunfo con otro 6-3. El desenlace de la jornada favoreció además a Sanz y Stupaczuk en su pugna por la cuarta posición de la tabla. Paquito Navarro y Martín Di Nenno no lograron asegurar su pase a semifinales tras ceder ante Momo González y Lucas Campagnolo. El sevillano y el argentino comenzaron con ventaja tras ganar el primer set por 6-2, pero González y Campagnolo remontaron el choque adjudicándose las dos siguientes mangas por 7-6 y 7-5, apretando la lucha por los puestos de cabezas de serie en la zona alta de la clasificación FIP.

articles.title: Penguins' Andrei Kuzmenko Switches Jersey Number to Honor Father Killed in Bear Attack
articles.summary: Pittsburgh Penguins forward Andrei Kuzmenko revealed that he changed his jersey number from No. 10 to No. 62 to honor his father, who was recently killed in a bear attack.
articles.body:
Pittsburgh Penguins forward Andrei Kuzmenko revealed that he changed his jersey number from No. 10 to No. 62 to honor his father, who was recently killed in a bear attack.

"My usual number is 96," Kuzmenko said Friday, via Josh Yohe of The Athletic. "I can't use it, and I understand No. 10, it's not important to me. I like it in my life and the big things. And now I understand this is my mother's birth year (of 1962) and my father, (was) 62 years (old) when he died. And today, we have (20)26 years. And I want to take 62 (as a) number."

Ranking Top 10 NCAA Men's Hockey Players for 2026-27 Season

Kuzmenko previously took a leave of absence from the team after his father was killed in a bear attack during a fishing trip in Siberia on Sept. 23.

He eventually returned to Pittsburgh's practice on Friday, as Penguins head coach Dan Muse was glad to see him back.

"He's obviously been in our thoughts here while he was away," Muse said, per Michelle Crechiolo of the team's official website. "We're really happy that he's back here – just being in the building, around his teammates, and getting to skate. It's tragic. We feel for him, his family, and thinking of them here over the past week. We're happy that he's back with his teammates."

Kuzmenko was appreciative of the support that he received on social media during his time away from the team.

"The next thing (is) about support," Kuzmenko said, via Yohe. "I want to say thank you for everyone who supported me. And I want to say thank you in the hockey world because I've seen the messages. A lot of information, everyone understands what happened because this is news and the whole word travels. And thank you (to) Russia. There's a lot of people who supported me. Thank you for everyone who supported me. And a lot of messages I see on Instagram. I'm sorry, I can't answer everyone. And I want to say thank you."

The 30-year-old is entering his fifth NHL season and his first with the Penguins, joining Pittsburgh on a one-year deal worth $5 million on July 1.

Kuzmenko suited up for the Los Angeles Kings during his 2025-26 campaign, recording 13 goals and 12 assists in 52 games played.

articles.title: World Grand Prix: Luke Humphries into semi-finals but Gian van Veen is knocked out by James Wade
articles.summary: Luke Humphries breezes into the semi-finals of the World Grand Prix with a comfortable 3-0 victory over Niels Zonneveld.
articles.body:
World number two Luke Humphries breezed into the semi-finals of the World Grand Prix with a 3-0 victory over Niels Zonneveld.

The Englishman did not quite hit top gear against the Dutchman - averaging 85.91 and throwing four 180s - but was clinical at the key moments with a checkout success of 33.33%.

Humphries has yet to drop a set in this year's tournament having whitewashed Dave Chisnall and Jermaine Wattimena in previous rounds.

The 31-year-old will face compatriot James Wade in the last four after he knocked out third seed Gian van Veen with a 3-0 win.

"The way I'm practising, I feel really good, it's just not been coming out this week. Against James, I know I need it to come out, it'll be a tough task," said Humphries, who won the tournament in 2023.

"To make four World Grand Prix finals on the trot would be super special. There's not many players that will ever do that and James will know he's got a tough game as well."

Elsewhere, Nathan Aspinall produced a stellar performance at Leicester's Mattioli Arena to secure his spot in the last four with a 3-0 victory over Ryan Joyce.

He will play Gerwyn Price in the semis after the Welshman's superb 3-2 comeback success against his compatriot Jonny Clayton, who spurned a two-set lead and match darts in a thrilling tie.

articles.title: World Grand Prix Darts: James Wade and Nathan Aspinall with statement displays ahead of semi-finals
articles.summary: James Wade faces Luke Humphries in final four after dropping just one leg in win over Gian van Veen; Nathan Aspinall averages 105.15 to set up Gerwyn Price meeting; watch the World Grand Prix semi-finals live on Saturday, from 8pm on Sky Sports+, 8.30pm on Main Event
articles.body:
Aspinall threatened to set a new tournament record average when storming to a 3-0 win over Ryan Joyce, his 105.15 mark ultimately landing as the fourth-highest in history and the best-ever in a quarter-final.

Wade, meanwhile, dropped only one leg as he, in his words, "bashed up" world No 2 Gian van Veen in a match that lasted little more than 20 minutes.

"That really was a performance to remember from Wade," Sky Sports ' Wayne Mardle said. "From start to finish, he was absolutely devastating. World Class."

Three-time world champion John Part concurred with that assesment, saying: "James is not just looking like a great dart thrower to me, he's looking like a winner.

"I really have a lot of faith in James managing the other players, and that's what winners do. They see what they have to work with, and work against.

"At the start of the match, James saw his opponent struggling and put his foot down to get the job done.

"I think he's a legitimate title contender here."

Humphries 'disappointed' despite clinching semi-final spot

Wade will face former world No 1 Luke Humphries in the final four, who was, by contrast, far from convincing despite the 3-0 scoreline from his quarter-final victory over debutant Neils Zonneveld.

Humphries averaged 85.91, the same as the Dutchmand, but his clutch doubling ultimately proved the difference as the 2023 champion reached the final four for a fourth-straight year.

Despite that, Humphries told Sky Sports afterwards: "I'm really disappointed. I felt really good in practice, but I came out here tonight and it didn't feel great to be honest.

"It kind of felt like I was the second-best player for the first two sets, but I got away with it.

"It's one of those performances where you're not thrilled, but I won 3-0.

"Hopefully tomorrow night is a lot better, because if it isn't I won't be here on Sunday."

Humphries added on his semi-final opponent: "James [Wade] is a tough task in itself. He's a tough player to play against.

"If I score the way I know I can, then it will be a tough night for James. If I don't, it's going to be a tough night for myself."

Aspinall thrilled by 'one of carrer-best performances'

Aspinall will face Price in Saturday's other semi-final after The Iceman came back from two sets down to beat Jonny Clayton in an all-Welsh affair, surving three match darts before edging the contest.

But it's Aspinall who is feeling particularly bullish going into a repeat of the 2022 semi-final, which The Asp won as he finished runner-up to Michael van Gerwen that year.

Aspinall's last major title came at the World Matchplay in 2023, but he's ready to change that.

"I feel like I can win this tournament, and I feel like I'm ready to win another major again. There's no reason why I can't," Aspinall told Sky Sports after his stunning quarter-final win over Joyce.

"I'm absolutely buzzing. All day I've felt so relaxed. I turned up tonight and felt so focussed.

"I'm really happy with that performance. My starting, my finishing, my 180s - it's probably one of my best performances ever on stage for my whole career."

OKLAHOMA CITY — After Oklahoma City Thunder's Shai Gilgeous-Alexander out-ran Jared McCain in a video that went viral during training camp, the third-year guard explained himself on Friday. Amidst McCain's first training camp with the Thunder , Jared addressed reporters for the first time since Media Day.

McCain reacted to Gilgeous-Alexander's dusting him in a video that went viral on X, formerly Twitter, per The Suave Report's Addam Francisco.

"Everybody's sending me that," McCain said, laughing. "No defending. It wasn't a race. What's funny is, right before I almost caught a cramp. articles.title: 49ers receiver Mike Evans listed as questionable but hopes to play Sunday
articles.summary: 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans, who exited last Sunday's game with a rib injury, is questionable for Sunday against the Broncos. Can he play with the pain? "...
articles.body:
Mike Evans has missed just 15 regular-season games over the first 12 years of his NFL career. The first-year San Francisco 49ers wide receiver frequently pops up on injury reports - he dealt with quad and adductor injuries during this year's training camp - but somehow, he nearly always manages to play on Sundays.

This time around, that might not be the case.

Evans, who suffered a rib injury in the 49ers' 36-30 win over the Arizona Cardinals last Sunday, is questionable for this Sunday's game against the Denver Broncos at Levi's Stadium. Head coach Kyle Shanahan said Evans will be a game-time decision. Evans was a limited participant in Friday's practice after he did not practice Wednesday or Thursday.

After running a route in the second quarter against Arizona, Evans went down in a heap despite not making contact with an Arizona defender. He struggled to get off the field, dropping to a knee and yelling in pain, before leaving on a cart.

Describing his injury Friday for the first time, Evans said: "That s- hurt bad. … When I ran a route and I turned, I just felt it. It felt like somebody stabbed me in my chest."

Evans said he didn't feel any pain until that play, but acknowledged the injury "might have happened before" then. On the 49ers' very first offensive play, Cardinals safety Budda Baker collided hard with Evans as he ran a route over the middle. He dropped to a knee and called to come off the field. "My head was ringing," Evans said, "but I didn't feel nothing in my chest or rib area."

He returned to the field two plays later and teamed up with Deebo Samuel for a hook-and-ladder touchdown. After Samuel's touchdown, Evans walked off the field rather somberly and took a seat on the 49ers' bench.

Evans said he has played through rib injuries during his career. Asked if he expects to play through this one, he responded: "I'll do my best."

General manager John Lynch called Evans a "tough SOB" and an "old school" player this week. Shanahan, who broke three ribs in his car accident in July, joked that he would not be questionable if he were in Evans' shoes.

"I would be out," Shanahan said, "without a doubt. But he's definitely a lot tougher than me, so hopefully we've got a shot."

articles.title: Steelers Host Former Bengals Edge Rusher for Visit
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers hosted veteran edge rusher Cam Sample for a free agent visit to UPMC Rooney Sports Complex on […]
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers hosted veteran edge rusher Cam Sample for a free agent visit to UPMC Rooney Sports Complex on Friday, according to the NFL transaction page.

Sample, 27, spent five seasons with the Cincinnati Bengals from 2021-25 after joining the Bengals as a fourth-round pick out of Tulane in 2021.

His contract with the Bengals expired this March, and he spent time with the San Francisco 49ers and Atlanta Falcons this offseason, but was released. In three preseason games with the Falcons this August, Sample had four tackles, one sack and two quarterback hits.

Sample was immediately a rotational player with the Bengals as a rookie in 2021. He played in 61 games over five years and made five starts, missing the entire 2024 season with a torn Achilles.

He has seven career sacks, eight tackles for loss and 26 quarterback hits, while recording 85 tackles. Sample's best statistical season was in 2022, when he recorded 25 tackles, two sacks, four tackles for loss and seven quarterback hits.

The Steelers do not have an obvious need at edge rusher, where four players earn significant playing time from the 53-man roster, and Bradyn Swinson and international pathway player Julius Welschof are on the practice squad.

In addition to hosting Sample for a visit, the Steelers also tried out four offensive linemen , two linebackers, a running back and a cornerback on Friday.

articles.title: Former WVU Football Star Is Having Dream Season With Neal Brown
articles.summary: The West Virginia Mountaineers have built their offense around the running game under Rich Rodriguez, but one former WVU star who could have made that backfi...
articles.body:
The West Virginia Mountaineers have built their offense around the running game under Rich Rodriguez, but one former WVU star who could have made that backfield even more dangerous is putting together a monster season elsewhere.

Former WVU running back Jahiem White delivered his biggest performance yet for North Texas, rushing 32 times for 219 yards and a touchdown in a wild 45-44 overtime victory over Tulsa. White produced 152 yards after contact and forced 10 missed tackles, continuing an impressive start to his next chapter playing for former West Virginia head coach Neal Brown.

White has now rushed for 582 yards and eight touchdowns through five games. He has scored 10 total touchdowns, making his reunion with Brown look increasingly successful. For WVU fans who watched White develop into one of the Mountaineers' most exciting offensive weapons, his production shouldn't be particularly surprising.

Ex-WVU RB Jahiem White Is Thriving With Neal Brown

White's departure from Morgantown wasn't exactly quiet. After entering the transfer portal, White publicly criticized aspects of Rodriguez's program during an Instagram Live broadcast. His decision eventually led him back to Brown, who coached White during his first two seasons at West Virginia. Now, White is thriving in his new home.

There is an important qualifier when comparing his North Texas production to what he could have done in the Big 12. The Mean Green don't face the same level of competition every week that West Virginia does, so White's numbers shouldn't simply be projected onto WVU's schedule. However, he has already shown this season that he can produce against elite competition.

North Texas opened the year against defending national champion Indiana, and White rushed 14 times for 61 yards and a touchdown. The Mean Green lost 52-16, but White still found success against one of the country's premier programs. That's what makes his breakout season difficult for WVU fans to ignore.

Rodriguez wants West Virginia to establish its identity on the ground. Cam Cook and quarterback Michael Hawkins Jr. have already provided significant production within that system, but imagining White alongside them creates a fascinating what-if for Mountaineers fans.

That relationship had run its course, though. White wanted a fresh start, and Brown offered him familiarity and another opportunity to become the centerpiece of an offense. So far, it has worked exceptionally well.

White's 219-yard explosion against Tulsa is the latest evidence that one of West Virginia's former stars hasn't simply found a new home. He has become one of North Texas' most productive offensive weapons and is having the type of season WVU fans always knew he was capable of producing.

articles.title: ‘Burnt Out’ Conor Benn Makes Huge Career Decision After Loss To Ryan Garcia
articles.summary: Conor Benn is burnt out after his second-round loss to Ryan Garcia and will never fight at welterweight again, says trainer Tony Sims. Middleweight could be...
articles.body:
Don't expect to see Conor Benn in the ring again any time soon. The UK boxing star's trainer Tony Sims says his fighter is "burnt out." Benn is seemingly done fighting at 147 pounds after a nasty weight cut and set for a lengthy layoff. Let's talk boxing.

Sept. 12, 2026, T-Mobile Arena, Las Vegas

Burnt out, needs a complete rest from boxing

Sims told Sky Sports , "I think he needs to have a rest from boxing completely at the moment." He also said a third fight with Eubank will still be there whenever Benn is ready, whether that's a year or a decade away.

Benn was destroyed by Garcia in the second round when the latter landed a titanic overhand right that scored a knockdown. Benn got to his feet, but Garcia swarmed him with a barrage of punches until the referee stepped in to call a halt to the fight.

Benn had spoken about a "brutal" weight cut during fight week and many including his rival Chris Eubank Jr. felt his performance was at least partially the result of him squeezing himself down to 147 pounds. In any case, that's probably not going to happen again. When Benn returns to the ring, he'll probably be fighting at 160 pounds or heavier and trying to recapture the power he once had.

Conor Benn's weigh-ins show how far he drifted from 147 before the Garcia fight.

As Sims mentioned, Benn has done well financially, so there's always the chance he could walk away from the sport entirely. While it is rare for a fighter of Benn's age, caliber and popularity to make that decision at this stage of their career, it's got to be considered whenever a fighter takes a long break from the sport.

Benn is also a warrior whose presence is good for the sport, but at the end of the day, he'll make the decision he believes is best for him.

articles.title: Chiefs Decision on Josh Simmons Backfires With Latest Injury Report
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs saw their preseason decision on Josh Simmons backfire as he missed a fourth straight game. The post Chiefs Decision on Josh Simmons Ba...
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs decided before the season to leave left tackle Josh Simmons off injured reserve, hoping that he would recover from a back injury and return in a few weeks.

That decision may have backfired, with the Chiefs now ruling out Simmons for a fourth straight game. The team announced that he would not play in this weekend's showdown against the Las Vegas Raiders, meaning he has already missed the equivalent of an injured reserve stint.

Chiefs head coach Andy Reid explained this week that Simmons has been dealing with a bulging disc in his lower back, which has "hindered the strength of his leg." Reid shared that Simmons has been making progress.

"He's working through it, he's here every day grinding away," Reid shared. "We didn't have to make any roster moves, so we didn't have to put him on IR (injured reserve). So, it's all worked out good that way. The positive is, though, he is making progress and getting stronger, which is important with those backs. As we know, backs can be a little tricky."

But had the Chiefs put Simmons on injured reserve just before the start of the regular season, they could have had an open roster spot while still losing him for the same amount of time. But Reid admitted that the team was uncertain of when he would return, making injured reserve a difficult decision.

"The timeline — that would be the other half of not putting him on IR — you never know with these things," Reid said. "We just hang in with it. The positive is he's here, and he's working and getting better."

Chiefs Get Some Good News on Josh Simmons

While it's not clear how much longer Simmons could be sidelined, Reid did have some good news about his prognosis. The Chiefs coach said he doesn't believe Simmons would require surgery, and still had a positive long-term outlook.

"I think we're headed in the right direction here, where it shouldn't happen," Reid said. "We'll see where it all goes. Knock on wood, I think we're going to be in a good place over time."

The Chiefs have not missed Simmons much over the first three games, going 3-0 with a rejuvenated offense. Running back Kenneth Walker III leads the league in rushing yards and yards from scrimmage, while quarterback Patrick Mahomes is having a throwback performance and near-perfect play on play-action passes that Walker has opened up.
