articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings ruled out Justin Jefferson for Week 4 against the Miami Dolphins after the wideout suffered an ankle injury in Week 3. As a result, the Vikings will look to move to 4-0 without their No. 1 receiver.

Nonetheless, in the NFL, it's a next-man-up mentality, and this is an opportunity for other receivers to step up. In the Week 3 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Jordan Addison elevated his game, recording five receptions for 90 yards and a touchdown.

On Oct. 2, Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell shared how he prepared his receivers as they look to replace the production lost with Jefferson's injury as a group for this game.

"We're going to call personnel groupings to get certain guys in the spots we want," O'Connell told reporters. "We've been able to practice it. It was some guys, including some of our young guys who have been here, like a Tai Felton or a Myles Price.

"It was their first time going through it a little bit, as well as Jauan [Jennings] being out there and being asked to do a little bit more than just maybe the position he's gotten the reps at throughout the week of a game plan. So across the board, I think everybody will be much more comfortable and I'm excited to see those guys play after the week of prep we just got out of those guys."

KOC Didn't Want to Risk Justin Jefferson's Homecoming

Meanwhile, O'Connell shared that Jefferson was progressing throughout the week and perhaps wanted to play it safe against the Dolphins, a team Minnesota should beat at him.

Furthermore, with the Vikings playing in Jefferson's home state against the New Orleans Saints , O'Connell probably didn't want to risk his wideout re-aggravating his ankle injury and missing that game.

"He's definitely feeling better," O'Connell added. "I think we're encouraged about where he's at, but just couldn't get there based on what you saw in practice next week. Yeah, obviously, we'll see how he comes in. He's going to get treatment throughout the next couple days, and the goal is to try to get him back out there practicing next week. I know it's a big one for him next week, going to Louisiana."

Vikings Are Fully Backing Kyler Murray Despite Concerns

As for the Minnesota offense, there are concerns about how Kyler Murray and the Vikings offense looked against Tampa Bay. Despite those concerns, Vikings edge rusher Dallas Turner has faith in the former No. 1 pick to lead them.

"I'll just say, Kyler is definitely a very, very athletic quarterback," Turner said during a Sept. 30 appearance on "Good Morning Football." "I kind of saw it during camp when I was trying to get a move around, and then you still have to tap off or try to just get near Kyler. This is doggone impossible, if you ask me, during practice.

"But definitely an athletic quarterback. You can tell he's a leader on the offensive side of the ball, and a lot of guys on the offensive side and on the defensive side trust him a lot."

articles.title: Rays’ ALDS Game 1 Starter Drew Rasmussen Coming Off Impressive Second Half
articles.summary: Tampa Bay's Drew Rasmussen made four starts against the Yankees this season. He went 2-1 with a 2.86 ERA while limiting Aaron Boone’s lineup to a.182 averag...
articles.body:
Drew Rasmussen was not on the active roster when the Rays last made the postseason in 2023. It was a season that came to an end for the righthander that May and he did not return to the mound again until the latter stages of the 2024 campaign.

Move ahead to October 2026 and the 31-year-old has the honor of starting Game 1 of the Tampa Bay's American League Division Series against the Yankees. The best-of-five series opens at Tropicana Field on Saturday evening.

"It's an honor, that's for sure," Rasmussen said Friday afternoon in the bowels of the Trop. "There are a lot of really good arms in (the Rays' clubhouse.) So, it is cool. I think they could have gone a number of different routes."

Manager Kevin Cash had that luxury. After all, Nick Martinez had a fantastic season and trade deadline acquisition Freddy Peralta was the American League's pitcher of the month for September. Rasmussen, though, has been a horse since the curtain rose on 2026 and scintillating since the all-star break, which was not a break for him because he was part of the AL squad in Philly.

"He was an all-star because of what he did in the first half and it's like he went out and doubled down and got even better," said Cash.

How much better? After a solid pre-break showing that included a 7-5 mark with a 3.26 ERA and impressive 0.95 WHIP, Rasmussen won all nine of his post-break decisions with a 1.86 ERA and 0.87 WHIP. The Rays won all 12 of his starts. His numbers for the season included 30 starts, an AL-best 0.91 WHIP, 16 wins (five losses) to place second in the AL, and a 2.67 ERA that was good for fourth in the junior circuit.

Among qualified pitchers, Martinez (1.30 BB/9) and Rasmussen (1.67 BB/9) were the stingiest in the majors when it came to free passes. All the while, Rasmussen largely maintained 94-96 mph on his fastball and 88-90 on his change. The latter was particularly effective.

"Generally, it is not unusual to see guys drop some in velocity from their 20 th to 30 th starts," said Cash. "I don't think 'Ras' has done that. The changeup is a pitch that really kind of developed for him on the fly. He's always had it, but the confidence to use it against certain hitters kind of grew in the (season's) second half from my vantage point."

Rasmussen made four starts against the AL East rival Yankees this season, going 2-1 with a 2.86 ERA while limiting Aaron Boone's lineup to a .182 average.

The 2025 season was one in which Rasmussen also partook of all-star festivities. He completed the season throwing 150 innings while his workload was closely monitored to help prevent anything resembling a setback in his first full season following the latest elbow procedure. Though Rasmussen did his part, he is immensely appreciative of those who helped get him back on the mound.

"A lot of people poured time, effort, and sweat into helping me get here," he said September 16, one day before his final regular season home start. "Just thinking about the rehab staff a couple of years ago, our strength staff, the people I worked with privately, there's been a lot of hours poured into this. In this game, individuals get to take a lot of credit for something that takes a village. I am happy to be on the field, and most of the time, positively impact our performance."

More like majority of the time. Rasmussen has allowed more than two runs, earned or otherwise, in only three of his last 19 starts. It is such consistency that stood out in a regular season that saw him pitch a career high 172 innings, and such consistency that impresses his teammates.

Yandy Diaz is one of only three players – also, Shane McClanahan and Taylor Walls -- on the 2026 Rays who were with the club when Rasmussen was acquired from Milwaukee in May 2021. The veteran appreciates what the pitcher went through to get to this point.

"There are not enough words to describe Drew Rasmussen," he said Friday via interpreter, Kevin Vera. "He's been great for us the entire year and he's someone who is dedicated to his work every single day. He does his job every single time he goes on the mound and pitches for us."

articles.title: WWE’s Roman Reigns reveals the truth of his battle with leukemia right now, ‘I have to be very careful’
articles.summary: Such is Roman Reigns’ superstar status in the WWE universe, that it’s easy to forget that this is very much a man battling a serious illness. Reigns has take...
articles.body:
Such is Roman Reigns' superstar status in the WWE universe, that it's easy to forget that this is very much a man battling a serious illness.

Reigns has taken breaks from WWE before to battle CML (Chronic myelogenous leukemia) and has fought back from that time away to build the Tribal Chief character into one of the greatest in WWE's long history.

Currently holding the WWE Heavyweight championship, Reigns is very much still at the top of his game and won't be going anywhere anytime soon.

However, while Reigns is in tip top shape and continuing to work a decent schedule with WWE, he has revealed how in reality, he still very much has to watch what he's doing.

Roman Reigns shares exactly where he is with his leukemia battle

The fact Reigns has elevated himself to such a level in WWE really is quite amazing given the battle he faces on a daily basis just to remain healthy.

Many will complain about his schedule or lack of matches but the reality is that Reigns – real name Joe Anoi'a – has to manage himself.

And while he's doing okay right now, Reigns has revealed that he's still not out of the woods just yet.

"Well, with my medical history, I have to be very careful," Reigns revealed in Men's Health magazine.

"You know, I'm still to this day, down to the wire, fighting CML. We're under control and we're under the actual baseline, but to be in molecular remission, it has to be almost zeroed out. And there's just still those minute traces, like 0.031, you know what I mean? But they count. So I still just have to be very careful and very smart."

Reigns has clearly and very bravely tackled this disease head on. It makes what he has achieved even more impressive and the longer it continues, the better.

Of course, the day might come where he has to make a decision. But for now, we are seeing one of the best of all-time do his thing and WWE are lucky to have Roman Reigns around.

articles.title: Cubs’ Michael Busch Gets Value $5.4 Million Contract Update
articles.summary: The Chicago Cubs have shifted gears into the offseason. They’d of course like to still be playing, but a futile hitting effort in the NL Wild Card Series at...
articles.body:
The Chicago Cubs have shifted gears into the offseason.

They'd of course like to still be playing, but a futile hitting effort in the NL Wild Card Series at the San Diego Padres ended that hope.

Instead, the Cubbies have to start considering what the roster will look like for next season.

The expectation is that it'll be different. The likes of Ian Happ, Seiya Suzuki, Kevin Gausman and Matthew Boyd are all bound for free agency, and they aren't guaranteed to return.

One guy who will be back is Michael Busch, the slugging first baseman.

He's one of a dozen Cubs who are due for the salary arbitration process this offseason, which allows for some projections on what a player might earn.

And if values come in as they potentially could, Busch could work out to be a bargain.

MLB Trade Rumors writer Matt Swartz has projected values for all the Cubs' arbitration eligible players.

The MLBTR projection for Busch's salary for the 2027 season comes in at $5.4 million.

At first glance, that feels like quite the good value for the Cubs.

That, in a lot of ways, is how the system is designed.

Each player that reaches the major leagues via the minor leagues has six years of club control once they reach the majors.

The first three years have a salary based on the collective bargaining agreement, and they're considered the pre-arbitration years.

Years four through six of a player's time with a team are the arbitration years. In each of those offseasons, a player is eligible to go to salary arbitration to determine what he's paid the following season.

The arbitration process features the team submitting a value and the player submitting one, and the independent arbitrator comes to a conclusion on which one wins out.

Teams and players in recent years often negotiate in advance to avoid actually going to what can be a contentious hearing, but the value they come out with will still end up close to what it would've been in arbitration.

All that said, it matters which year a player is in for the sequence — and this is only Busch's first arbitration year. Generally, the first arbitration year comes with the lowest salaries, and they rise in each of the two subsequent years, even if the player is viewed as having exactly the same value each season.

That means that Busch wasn't going to end up with a huge value no matter what he did this season.

The best he can do is get a solid salary this offseason and try to keep building for years ahead — unless the Cubs want to sign him to a contract extension that buys out some of his free agent years and gets him a better payday now.

The Cubs have 12 players eligible for salary arbitration this offseason, including Busch.

The full dozen: Justin Steele, Edward Cabrera, Braxton Garrett, Javier Assad, Tyler Austin, Miguel Amaya, Gabriel Arias, Ryan Rolison, Ethan Roberts, Michael Busch, Ben Brown, Daniel Palencia.

The Cubs don't have to keep all those players. They can opt to non-tender someone (not offer him a contract), and that sends them instead straight to free agency.

articles.title: Two Bayern Munich Frauen mainstays struck down with injury
articles.summary: FC Bayern will be missing a pair of starters for tomorrow’s big Bundesliga clash at Eintracht Frankfurt.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich travels to face Eintracht Frankfurt in a huge matchup at the top of the Frauen-Bundesliga table this weekend, but the Bavarians will need to make do without two of coach José Barcala's regular starters.

Striker Jovana Damnjanović and defender Vanessa Gilles are both out with what are being described as 'muscular issues', per information from the club's website, FCBayern.com .

Damnjanović had featured in Bayern's Champions League win over SL Benfica on Wednesday but was withdrawn in the second half after staying down on the turf following a clattering of bodies. She was replaced in the match by attacking midfielder Alara in a move that allowed Danish forward Pernille Harder to lead the line. Sarah Zadrazil's recent return from her own injury gives Bayern another central midfield option that could see Momoko Tanikawa move into the No. 10 position, while new transfer Sophie Proost is another option among the forwards. Proost, 19, has appeared largely in substitute appearances on the wings.

Gilles did not play in the UWCL in favor of the recently returned Stine Ballisager. The Canadian international has been a force this season, particularly from set pieces. Gilles has scored three goals in the Frauen-Bundesliga already and added a critical brace in Bayern's nervy 2-1 DFB-Pokal First Round win over Borussia Mönchengladbach.

Bayern and Frankfurt are 1-2 in the league table, with Frankfurt coming off a 6-1 cup win over Karlsruher SC.

articles.title: Steelers Co-Owner Robert Citrone Loses Bid to Stop Amy Blunt From Speaking Publicly About Child Support Fight
articles.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers co-owner Robert Citrone has lost his bid for an emergency order restricting what Amy Blunt can say publicly about their ongoing child sup...
articles.body:
Pittsburgh Steelers co-owner Robert Citrone has lost his bid for an emergency order restricting what Amy Blunt can say publicly about their ongoing child support dispute.

A Pennsylvania judge denied Citrone's request after his lawyers sought to prevent Blunt from discussing the case with journalists or posting about it on social media, according to a court order obtained by TMZ .

Citrone's attorneys had pointed to posts Blunt allegedly made about his finances and their 3-year-old son, as well as statements indicating that she planned to discuss the dispute on TikTok.

The ruling leaves the larger child support case unresolved. Blunt is seeking financial information that she argues is relevant to determining support, while the underlying proceedings remain sealed.

Citrone Wanted Blunt Barred From Posting About the Case

Citrone's emergency request followed a social media post that his attorneys said discussed developments in the litigation and made claims about his wealth and level of financial support.

In a Sept. 25 filing, his legal team also said Blunt had told her attorney that she intended to create a TikTok account where she would discuss what she characterized as Citrone's infidelity and his alleged failure to adequately support their son.

Blunt opposed the proposed restriction, arguing that Citrone was objecting to the substance of what she wanted to say rather than identifying a valid basis for preventing her from speaking publicly.

Her response also argued that restricting former romantic partners from discussing their personal lives would improperly limit protected speech.

The Judge Kept the Seal in Place Without Imposing a Broader Gag Order

The judge denied Citrone's emergency motion but emphasized that the case itself remains sealed.

Neither side may distribute sealed filings to people who are not involved in the litigation. The court order also states that no separate gag order currently prevents Citrone or Blunt from speaking about the dispute unless they mutually agree to one.

That means both sides can speak publicly about the dispute, but they still cannot share court materials that remain under seal.

The Child Support Fight Includes a Dispute Over Citrone's Finances

In earlier court documents, Blunt sought Citrone's tax returns, income statements and information about his family's standard of living. TMZ reported that she alleged Citrone had $113 million in taxable income in 2024 and argued that his financial circumstances should be considered when the court determines an appropriate level of support.

A judge allowed Blunt to take depositions of Citrone, his wife and his children regarding their standard of living. Citrone's attorneys later cited Blunt's public discussion of that development when seeking the emergency speech restriction.

The filings also describe the couple's young son as having significant medical needs. Because the case concerns a minor, the court proceedings themselves remain sealed.

Citrone Has Been Part of the Steelers Ownership Group for Years

Citrone is a hedge fund manager who has held an ownership stake in the Pittsburgh Steelers for more than a decade.

The Pittsburgh Post-Gazette previously reported that Citrone and his wife, Cindy, joined the Steelers ownership group after being approached about investing in the franchise and later increased their stake.

Citrone grew up in western Pennsylvania and has also been involved in philanthropic projects in the Pittsburgh area.

articles.title: Army hockey - Black Knights counting on better, consistent play
articles.summary: Army hockey head coach Zach McKelvie believes a consistent approach, with improved talent, will move the Black Knights forward in 2026-27.
articles.body:
The rebuild of the Army hockey team is well on its way.

"We really like the group that we have,'' second-year head coach and alum Zach McKelvie said. "We feel like we're a deeper team. We've got a lot of good talent up front, and obviously a good goalie coming back, so we're optimistic, but we are a little bit green because we have 12 new freshmen this year.''

The Black Knights (last season 12-17-6 overall; ninth place out of 10 in Atlantic Hockey America) figure to provide more scoring from four lines, roll out more experienced special teams and feature junior goaltender J.J. Cataldo, considered one of the best players in the league. Also, junior Jack Ivey was named to the preseason all-conference team.

Army was picked to finish seventh (of nine) in the preseason coaches' poll, and McKelvie expects the entire circuit to be closer than ever.

"Last summer ... we created a three- or four-year plan, and we knew it's going to take time,'' McKelvie said, citing Army's inability to tap into the NCAA transfer portal like other schools. "We knew we were going to have to build it from the ground up — the traditional way — and we like that because it helps our culture.

"We're excited about this year and the coming years. We feel like we can make a noticeable jump this year because of the group we have, and we got to learn from some of the things that we did last year, and largely that was an inconsistency thing ... it wasn't a talent thing, and now we have more talent.''

Year two of the McKelvie era begins this weekend against a pair of ECAC members: RPI visits Friday for an exhibition, and Union visits Saturday for the regular-season opener.

Cataldo started 32 games last season, playing all but three contests. He posted a .921 save percentage and 2.48 goals against average. McKelvie likes backups Jacob Biron and Gus Holt but plans to ride Cataldo as long as he holds up. Count on Biron, Holt and freshman Owen Crudale to see time in three October exhibitions with RPI, Canada's Royal Military College and the U.S. National Development Under-18 team.

Army's top line features playmaker Nils Forselius and creative twins Jack Ivey and Ben Ivey, three different types of players who complement one another. McKelvie said Jack Ivey plays with a "ton of confidence" and is asserting himself more as a leader.

Freshman Rhys Wallin joins center Barron Woodring and Brent Keefer on the second unit — the latter duo play on the power play and penalty kill. Woodring plays physically, is good defensively and has a good goal-scoring touch. The speedy Keefer has a solid outside shot. A long and lanky Wallin has speed and plays similarly to his linemates.

The versatile Nik Hong — a captain with Woodring and Easton Zueger — has good net presence and centers a third unit that has shown the most consistency during preseason. Creative left winger Billy Batten has made the biggest jump since last season. A tenacious worker, freshman Sean Gibbons played his way into a right winger job.

Freshman Thomas Quast has been very consistent on the top defensive pairing with Lukas McCloskey, a duo expected to play 20-22 minutes per game in every situation, McKelvie said. Liam Chapman steadily increased his minutes last season with his ability to "lean on" skaters, and offensive-minded Pierce Patterson has the best one-timer shot on the blue line. Seniors Jon Bell and Easton Zueger provide an experienced pairing that will do "whatever that is asked of them,'' McKelvie said. Noah Mertz is a freshman who will find time because of his ability to run the power play.

"We want to be a team that can play fast, so that means our (defense) has to get back on pucks quick and get it up to the forwards as fast as possible,'' McKelvie said, hoping to pick up the transition from last year's group.

Army is coming off a truncated preseason camp, altered due to ice cooling system renovations at Tate Rink — not only did the Black Knights lose valuable individual practice time for the first three weeks of the academic calendar, but the team had to utilize ice time in Newburgh and Monsey to get in work before Tate was ready.

articles.title: Rams rule out Aaron Donald, place Terrance Ferguson on IR and waive Xavier Smith
articles.summary: WOODLAND HILLS, Calif.
articles.body:
WOODLAND HILLS, Calif. — The Rams will be without defensive tackle Aaron Donald on Sunday because of back soreness, placed tight end Terrance Ferguson on injured reserve and waived wide receiver and return specialist Xavier Smith as they try to rebound from a 1-2 start.

Speaking before practice Friday, coach Sean McVay said Donald experienced soreness after last week's loss to the Denver Broncos that had not improved as the team hoped. McVay characterized the decision to hold him out as a matter of protecting a player who would otherwise try to play through the discomfort.

"He's as tough as it gets, but just not feeling good enough," McVay said. "He would do it and he could probably go be productive, but part of our job is to protect these tough dudes like him from themselves and that's what went into the decision."

McVay said the decision came after discussions with Reggie Scott, the Rams' senior vice president of sports medicine and performance. He did not provide a timetable for Donald's return, but said Donald was doing everything possible to get healthy.

"You guys know him, he's working as hard as he can to get himself feeling as good as possible," McVay said. "We're hopeful and optimistic that good days are ahead."

Donald's absence adds to the uncertainty surrounding a defense that is also waiting for Myles Garrett to return. McVay said Garrett is making progress in his rehabilitation and has been participating in meetings, but he was not ready to offer a specific timeline.

The Rams also ruled out cornerback Jaylen Watson. Outside linebacker Josaiah Stewart is questionable because of groin soreness, while tight end Colby Parkinson did not practice Friday and is questionable, leaving the Rams with additional concerns at tight end following Ferguson's move to injured reserve.

There was better news for the offense: Wide receiver Puka Nacua is cleared to play. McVay said Nacua looked sharp during Thursday's practice, the team's heaviest workload of the week, although the Rams will monitor his conditioning and determine how to handle his snap count.

"He's good to go," McVay said. "I think physically he's getting in and out of his breaks, looks strong, looks sturdy, looks explosive."

The decision to waive Smith, meanwhile, reflected McVay's dissatisfaction with the return game. McVay said the move was made Thursday night and communicated to Smith on Friday morning, explaining that the Rams needed better production and decision-making at the position.

"We just need better production out of that position," McVay said. "That's exclusively what it was."

McVay expressed appreciation for Smith's journey and their relationship, but said his responsibility was to make decisions that benefited the entire team. He pointed to problems in last week's game without detailing individual plays.

"We have to make better decisions. We have to be able to field it," McVay said. "It doesn't mean that I love him any less, but we need better production from that position that he was playing a critical factor in."

Practice squad receiver Alex Bachman emerged as the leading candidate to take over return duties. McVay said running back Kyren Williams was another trusted option, but he would prefer to avoid adding that responsibility to his starting running back.

"There are candidates, but Bachman would be the guy in the immediate future that we feel good about," McVay said.

McVay left open the possibility of exploring other return options, while expressing optimism about what Bachman could provide Sunday. The change is part of a broader effort to get all three phases working together after the Rams lost two of their first three games.

"This story is not yet written," McVay said. "We've got a lot of ball ahead of us, but we have to start doing what we can on a daily basis, and that's what I've seen from this group this week which I've been really encouraged with."

articles.title: 5 ways the Oklahoma Sooners offense needs to get back on track
articles.summary: If the Oklahoma Sooners offense is going to get back on track, these 5 things have to get right.
articles.body:
The Oklahoma Sooners ' offense struggled in the final three weeks of September. After putting up 51 points in the season-opening win over UTEP, Oklahoma has averaged 12.3 points per game against Michigan, New Mexico, and Georgia.

The Sooners' defense gives Oklahoma a shot in every game. But it can't do everything. The offense needs to provide something and they've got the playmakers to do it. But what are some things that need to get right for the Sooners to find some success, score points, and win games moving forward? Here are five things that can help.

Not everything that's gone on with the Oklahoma Sooners offense is entirely on John Mateer. But if he comes out of the bye week better, that helps tremendously.

Most of what needs to happen is regaining his confidence. Peyton Bowen called it his "mojo ." If he finds his mojo and regains his confidence, Mateer could be the one to turn the offense around. He needs to throw the ball on time and take shots downfield to soften up defenses. If he lacks confidence, he'll keep second-guessing what he sees. Oklahoma's offense has throws to be made, but Mateer looks to be second-guessing what he sees after he hits his drop.

The Oklahoma Sooners haven't had one of their best players for the first month of the season as left tackle Michael Fasusi has been dealing with a shoulder injury suffered in fall camp. He tried to play through the issue against UTEP but was severely limited and hasn't played since.

Fasusi is your best offensive lineman and his presence would not only provide an upgrade at left tackle, but it would also allow Bill Bedenbaugh to shift Ryan Fodje back to his more natural right tackle spot and then work with Heath Ozaeta, Eddy Pierre-Louis, Noah Best, and E'Marion Harris to find the best guard combination for either side of Jake Maikkula.

Right now the Sooners have too many questions along the offensive line for it to be successful, but Fasusi's presence would help a lot.

A lot of the offensive conversation over the last week has focused on Mateer after three straight weeks of turnover-laden games. As much as he needs to improve, the Oklahoma offense has to find some help for him via the running game.

Oklahoma's rushing attack is averaging 99 yards per game through four games, which ranks No. 129 in the nation. Only two Power Four teams are averaging fewer rushing yards per game than the Sooners: Stanford and Arkansas. Oklahoma's 2.9 yards per attempt ranks 134th out of 138 teams.

For a program that spent the offseason working to improve the running game, they've taken a step backward.

Now, the run game will take a step forward if Mateer finds some consistency throwing the ball downfield. It'll also be aided if Fasusi can get back in action.

Isaiah Sategna is your best offensive weapon, but Rocky Beers isn't far behind. Beers is second on the team in receptions and yards with 18 catches for 255 yards and two touchdowns. When he's targeted, good things happen. Beers is making the reception on 81.8% of his targets.

But it's been an up-and-down target share for the Sooners' dynamic tight end. In games one and three, he only had two targets. In games two and four, Beers had nine targets in each game.

Mateer feels most comfortable throwing over the middle of the field, and Beers provides the Sooners with a dynamic weapon in that area of the passing game. He should have a high target share moving forward and be involved on every critical down.

The Oklahoma Sooners have weapons in the wide receiver corps. Sategna, Elijah Thomas, Jahsiear Rogers, and others can create in space with the ball in their hands. As an extension of the running game, Oklahoma needs to find ways to get them more involved in the quick passing game. Whether on slants, drag routes, or wide receiver screens. Find ways to get your most electric playmakers the ball in space and force defenses to defend you sideline to sideline.

The Sooners need to find some success down the field to get defenses to back away from the line of scrimmage, which would open up the running game a bit more. But also, if teams are forced to defend the screen a bunch, they'll be more susceptible to deep shots.

articles.title: Northwestern University's new Ryan Field debuts with game against Penn State, ushers in new era
articles.summary: Northwestern University prepared to open a new chapter in its football history Friday night with the debut of the new Ryan Field, a stadium that replaces the...
articles.body:
Northwestern University prepared to open a new chapter in its football history Friday night with the debut of the new Ryan Field, a stadium that replaces the venue that traces its roots back 100 years.

Parents, alumni and fans gathered for pregame tailgating ahead of the first game at the new facility. Outside the stadium, workers were still putting the finishing touches on the project as opening time approached.

"It's fantastic. They've been down to the wire working really hard," said neighbor Mark Hansen, who has watched construction since it began.

The original stadium opened 100 years ago as Dyche Stadium and was renamed Ryan Field in 1997. For many longtime fans, the debut of the new stadium marked a significant milestone.

Season ticket holder Josh Denlow said he has been attending games for five decades.

"We hung out here like it was a playground at the old Dyke Stadium and then Ryan Field. Never could I imagine what this is today," Denlow said.

The new stadium is set to welcome a sellout crowd of 35,000 fans. That is about 12,000 fewer seats than the previous Ryan Field, but the facility was designed to bring fans closer to the action with a more vertical seating configuration intended to provide strong sightlines throughout the stadium.

"This is a college town. So when you have a facility like this who can entertain the best of the best and play outstanding football, it helps the community," said Northwestern fan Michael Mitchell.

The project cost about $850 million, making it one of the most expensive college stadiums in the country. University officials have also planned a number of surprises for the opening-night festivities.

Even some family members of players said they were unsure what to expect.

"I'm not sure what's gonna happen. There could be fireworks. John Bon Jovi, jumping out. Not sure. We're excited to see them out on the field," said Kristen Carsello, a parent.

Northwestern was scheduled to host Penn State in the stadium's inaugural game. Kickoff was set for 7 p.m., with the game nationally televised. University officials encouraged fans to arrive early for pregame festivities and planned surprises.

articles.title: Red Wings' Dylan Larkin booed by fans after trade request
articles.summary: Detroit Red Wings star Dylan Larkin, who has requested a trade, wasn't playing because of an injury. But he heard boos when introduced.
articles.body:
Detroit Red Wings star Dylan Larkin received a big reaction from fans as he appeared at Little Caesars Arena amid his trade request.

Larkin wasn't playing on Friday, Oct. 2 because of an upper body injury but he was introduced along with the other players who weren't dressed. He gave a wave to fans after the reaction.

Unlike Winnipeg Jets goalie Connor Hellebuyck, who is suspended for not reporting , Larkin agreed to report to training camp . But he missed the early practices because he was hurt while training in the offseason.

The Red Wings placed him on the injured list retroactive to Aug. 15 and he will miss this weekend's games.

Larkin made the trade request after the 2025-26 season, in which Detroit missed the playoffs for a 10th consecutive season. Efforts to trade him were complicated because Steve Yzerman stepped aside as general manager . Shawn Horcoff was named interim GM .

Larkin has five years left on his contract at an $8.7 million cap hit. The longtime captain lost his "C" and the Red Wings will start the season without a captain.

The Detroit Free Press, part of the USA TODAY Network, reported that Larkin has increased his list of teams where he'd accept a trade.

In addition to the Florida Panthers, Minnesota Wild and Vegas Golden Knights, Larkin's list now includes the Colorado Avalanche, Dallas Stars , Tampa Bay Lightning and Washington Capitals.

Contributing: Helene St. James, Detroit Free Press

articles.title: Joe Mazzulla Reveals Reason Behind Celtics’ Citadel Training Camp
articles.summary: Joe Mazzulla wanted his revamped Celtics roster to experience something different during training camp.
articles.body:
The Boston Celtics are trading their usual training-camp routine for something a little different.

Boston is heading to South Carolina on Saturday for a three-day stay at The Citadel Military College of South Carolina. The Celtics will practice there before returning home ahead of their preseason opener against the Cleveland Cavaliers next Thursday.

The decision gives Boston a chance to break away from its normal surroundings as it prepares for a season with plenty of new faces.

Fourth-year head coach Joe Mazzulla believes that's exactly what his team needs.

"It's always good to shake it up a little bit," Mazzulla said during a practice interview . "This is my fifth training camp and the first four were here, so we're just looking to do something a little different."

Mazzulla has previously spoken about how much he values lessons from military leadership. He sees the trip as an opportunity for the Celtics to incorporate some of those principles while strengthening the team's relationships away from the basketball court.

"I really enjoy military leadership. I've learned from it a lot," Mazzulla told the Boston Globe. "I think it's important, so any chance that we could get to do it, we'll try."

Team-building has been part of Boston's approach before, and Mazzulla indicated that the Celtics have previously worked with military personnel in that area. This time, the entire team will get the chance to experience the setting firsthand.

The Celtics' decision to leave Boston comes at a significant point in their preparation. With a revamped roster and several players adjusting to new roles, Mazzulla is using training camp to establish more than just Boston's on-court systems.

The trip to The Citadel gives the Celtics a different setting to work on those connections before the preseason begins.

articles.title: Ohio State vs. Iowa Buckeyes Wire staff predictions for CFB Week 5
articles.summary: Ohio State travels to take on Iowa on Saturday and our writers each took turns predicting the outcome of the game in Iowa City.
articles.body:
We've got a fairly sizeable matchup Saturday in Iowa City as Ohio State visits for a top-15 contest. Ohio State's only loss is to No. 1 Texas , and Iowa is undefeated after upsetting Michigan last week in Ann Arbor. The two will clash among the cornfields of the Hawkeye State, with the winner still undefeated and on track in the Big Ten , and the loser with less room for error for the rest of the season.

Each week, we like to ask our writers to predict the outcome of that week's Ohio State game, and with this one being one that even College GameDay is on campus for, there's a little more buzz to get the prediciton machines going.

So what do Phil, Mark, Sunny, and Alec have to say about who will win between Ohio State and Iowa? Do they all have the same outcome, or is someone going against the grain? Here's what all four writers believe will happen Saturday afternoon inside Kinnick Stadium.

Ohio State vs. Illinois, according to Phil Harrison, Lead Writer/Editor

It's so hard to go to Iowa and play your own game. The Hawkeyes do such a great job of mucking things up and making you play their type of contest with slow play, defense, field position, and special teams. But that's more at night than it is in the afternoon for some reason in Iowa City, and it's hard to see the Iowa defense being able to slow down the Buckeyes ' passing game more often than not. It still will be a dogfight with Ohio State having to settle for field goals at times instead of touchdowns, but the good guys come out with a solid win on the road against a good defensive team.

Score Prediction: Ohio State 26, Iowa 20

Ohio State vs. Illinois, according to Mark Russell, Featured Writer

Playing at Kinnick is never easy, and the crowd will be even more hyped with College GameDay in town. While the Iowa pass defense has been one of the best in the nation, they haven't faced the likes of the Ohio State passing attack. Iowa may be able to move the ball on the ground against a Buckeye front seven that is still trying to figure out an identity, but I don't think it will be enough. Ultimately, if Julian Sayin has time, he'll find Jeremiah Smith and others to move the ball.

Score Prediction: Ohio State 31, Iowa 17

Ohio State vs. Illinois, according to Sunny Verma, Featured Writer

Iowa is coming off an energetic last-second victory over Michigan at home, and Iowa City is hosting ESPN Gameday, so you know the campus is buzzing. In reality, how good Michigan truly is still up in the air, and we will have a better idea by the end of the season how impressive that win actually was. Ohio State put up over 500 yards on the Illinois defense the previous week, and the Sayin-to-Smith connection rolls on.

Score Prediction: Ohio State 31, Iowa 13

Ohio State vs. Illinois, according to Alec Lasley, Featured Writer

Ohio State is looking to avenge a road loss to Texas earlier this year and go on the road for the second time and come away with a gritty win. Playing in Iowa City is never easy, and this is an Iowa team that has a lot of confidence coming off last week's win against Michigan on the last play of the game. There's a bit more offensive punch than usual, but it's the same hard-nosed defense. The line of scrimmage needs to be won on both sides of the ball by OSU. Last week was the first game it was able to establish the running game early, and I expect the same mindset this week. Iowa knows it can't stop Jeremiah Smith, but it does seem to have a good understanding of how it'll try to slow him down or adjust for him. This will be closer than people think, but I do believe the Buckeyes pull it out late.

articles.title: Watch Yankees’ Aaron Judge take batting practice before ALDS roster decision
articles.summary: Junior Caminero and Ben Rice posted MVP-caliber campaigns in 2026. Cam Schlittler and Drew Rasmussen amazed fans and smothered hitters from the mound. Bryan...
articles.body:
Junior Caminero and Ben Rice posted MVP-caliber campaigns in 2026. Cam Schlittler and Drew Rasmussen amazed fans and smothered hitters from the mound. Bryan Baker and David Bednar did the same from the closer role. Trade deadline additions Liam Hicks and Luis Garcia Jr. have both made an impact. There is much to unpack in this upcoming American League Division Series between the Tampa Bay Rays and New York Yankees , and yet, the biggest question centers around a man who has only played 66 games this year. Will Aaron Judge step up to the plate this weekend?

Although the Yankees have yet to release their final ALDS roster, the three-time MVP is seemingly getting himself ready for playoff baseball. Judge looked quite sharp while taking batting practice on Friday evening, per Jon Heyman of the New York Post and MLB Network. New York left him off the team for its Wild Card Series versus the Boston Red Sox and cruised to a 2-0 series sweep after some puzzling pitching choices by the opposition, but the circumstances are different now.

Tampa Bay owns home-field advantage and ended the season far better than the Sox did. Judge could be an equalizer. Though, he could also complicate the Yankees' defensive configuration . The generational superstar is recovering from a calf strain and could therefore be limited in the outfield.

If manager Aaron Boone inserts his captain into the designated hitter role, he would presumably shift Rice to first base, Garcia to second and Jazz Chisholm Jr. to third. Aaron Judge in right field is the optimal scenario, but it is unclear just how mobile he is following his latest stint on the injured list.

His bat seems fine, though, and if that is the case, then it is hard to foresee New York keeping No. 99 out of action for any longer. An official decision will be made before the Rays and Yankees duke it out on Saturday night.
